newsitem.title: USA: NY PRECIOUS METALS END MOSTLY HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: NY PRECIOUS METALS END MOSTLY HIGHER.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Thursday, after expectations for more losses were confounded early by continued buying by one or two investment banks, forcing locals and funds to cover short positions.
"Its pretty nervous out there, people are a little bit confused at these levels (in gold)," Credit Lyonnais Rouse New York chief bullion dealer Scott Mehlman said.
"Overall the market is still looking for lower prices, but people are less willing to stick their necks out on the short side until things settle down a bit," he said.
"Gold looks like its trying to build a base around $320 (in COMEX December gold), with $317-318 on the bottom and $324-325 on the top and I wouldn't be surprised to see any of those prices trade."
Goldman Sach's continued to be the main buyer supporting COMEX gold futures, though was seen on the offer in the cash market, many traders said.
In late July, Goldman Sachs handled the 1.1 million ounce hedge buy back for Newmont Mining.
COMEX December gold ended up $3.30 at $325.80 an ounce, after holding above the lows of the past two days on the open and taking out Wednesday's highs at $324.80.
COMEX gold estimated total volume was moderate at 38,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $321.70/20, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $321.00 and the New York close Wednesday around $318.30/80.
Implied gold lease rates were steady around 1.77 pct for one month, after edging back up Wednesday from a four week low around 1.54 pct Tuesday.

North American gold equities, sometimes a leading indicator for the gold price, continued to recover Thursday, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's gold and silver mining sector index (.XAU) edging up to a session high at 99.05 points, its highest level since June 20.
COMEX September silver ended 4.2 cents at $4.375 an ounce, after finding some support Wednesday around $4.30, following a slide earlier in the week from over $4.50.
The spot gold/silver ratio was little changed around 73.2-to-1.
NYMEX platinum and palladium futures also found some support after two days of sharp falls.

NYMEX October platinum ended up $1.60 at $432.60 an ounce, after holding above Wednesday's lows at $424.60, but the October/January spread eased further to $9.00 an ounce, and the October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread slipped back to $108.30 an ounce from a high at $129.20 earlier this week.
NYMEX September palladium ended down $3.10 an ounce at $212.50, but was off the session's worst levels at $205.25.
One month platinum lease rates eased to about 15-20 pct early Wednesday, but one month palladium lease rates rose to around 90 pct.

The sharp downward correction in PGM prices this week was not unexpected, analysts said, as PGM prices had rallied quickly in July, taking palladium prices back up to 17 year highs and platinum prices back up to near the seven year highs seen June.
But there was still an acute shortage of metal in the physical market, which was not being alleviated by the modest amounts of metal coming out of Russia.
Russia resumed exports of PGMs last month, after a six month suspension.
